claim: Van Gogh was institutionalized at Saint-Paul-de-Mausole from 8 May 1889 to 16 May 1890; visitors today see the cloister, chapel, Roman promenades, and a reconstructed Van Gogh bedroom.
quote: 8 mai 1889 au 16 mai 1890 ... la chambre de Van Gogh ... le cloître et les chemins botaniques, chapelle et clocher, promenades romaines, galerie Valetudo

claim: During his 53-week stay Van Gogh produced 143 oil paintings and over 100 drawings including The Starry Night, Irises, Olive Orchard, and Wheat Field with Cypresses; the monastery still functions as a psychiatric institution and houses an active art-therapy studio.
quote: he carried out 143 oil paintings and more than 100 drawings in the space of 53 weeks ... The Irises, Starry Night, Olive Orchard, Wheat field with Cypress, and Garden in the St-Paul hospice

claim: Saint-Paul-de-Mausole is open daily from 9 Feb 2026 through 3 Jan 2027; winter hours 10:15-12 and 13-17:15 (last entry 16:30), summer hours from 1 April 9:30-19:00 (last entry 18:30); 2026 entry fee €10.
quote: From February 9, 2026 until January 3, 2027 ... From February 8 to March 31: 10:15 AM to 12 PM and 1 PM to 5:15 PM ... From April 1 onwards: 9:30 AM to 7 PM ... EUR 10

claim: Glanum is a Greco-Roman city (capital of the Glaniques, flourished under Rome until ~270 AD) with columned villas, forum, thermal baths and mosaics; full-price entry €9, audioguide €3; April-September open daily 9:30-18:00.
quote: Glanum is an ancient archaeological site ... Full price: €9.00 ... April 1–September 30: 9:30 AM–6 PM ... last admission 45 minutes before closing

claim: Les Antiques — the Mausoleum of the Julii (30-20 BC) and the Triumphal Arch (the oldest in France, Augustan era) — stand on an open esplanade about 1 km south of town and are freely accessible at any time of day, classified national monuments since 1840.
quote: the Mausoleum and the oldest triumphal arch in France ... classified as national monuments in 1840 ... freely accessible at any time of day. Les Antiques never closes

claim: The Saint-Rémy Provençal market runs every Wednesday 8:00-13:00 year-round on Place de la République and through the historic centre, with hundreds of stalls of herbs, olives, oils, produce, honey, flowers, linens, lavender and crafts.
quote: every Wednesday between 8 am and 1 pm ... Place de la République and in the streets of the historic centre ... herbs, spices, olives, oils, fruits, vegetables, honeys, flowers

claim: A smaller Saturday morning market also runs 8-13; the pedestrianised old town offers art galleries, cafés and ice-cream parlours and a day is enough to cover the main sights.
quote: Market days in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence are on Wednesday and Saturday, from 8am to 1pm ... you likely only need a day in St. Rémy de Provence

claim: Nostradamus (Michel de Nostredame) was born in 1503 at 6 rue Hoche in the old town; a fountain at the corner of rue Carnot and rue Nostradamus and a zodiac fresco on Boulevard Mirabeau commemorate him.
quote: born in 1503 in the family home at 6 rue Hoche ... fountain dedicated to Nostradamus at the corner of rue Carnot and rue Nostradamus ... colourful fresco of Nostradamus and a zodiac

claim: Musée Estrine occupies an 18th-century Provençal hôtel particulier in the old town and houses the Van Gogh Interpretation Centre; the experience is interpretive (panels and a lyrical French-language film) rather than original-painting-heavy, with a 20th/21st-century collection of 1000+ works.
quote: former 18th century mansion ... interpretive rather than object-heavy, with display panels and a lyrical film (in French) ... more than 1000 works

claim: Free parking lots ring the old town (Boulevard Marceau, Place de la République, Avenue Frédéric Mistral, Parking de la Libération); on Wednesday market days arrive before 9 a.m. or use the free shuttle from the Petite Crau car park (every 15 min, 9:00-13:00).
quote: main parking lot is on Boulevard Marceau ... Parking de la Libération ... arrive before 9 a.m. ... free shuttle bus service from the Petite Crau car park between 9am and 1pm, running every 15 minutes

claim: Spring (April-May) and autumn (September-October) are the best seasons — pleasant temperatures, strong Provençal light, fewer crowds; Wednesday morning is the recommended day to catch the full market atmosphere.
quote: Spring (April-May) and autumn (September-October) offer the best conditions: pleasant temperatures, magnificent light and fewer tourists ... Wednesday mornings are recommended to coincide with market day
